goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing 'embedding' in ADMIN_MODELS causes basePath to return '/', producing malformed '//admin/customize/embedding' scheme-relative URL so the admin Embedding page fails to load and saveChanges PUT never reaches Admin::EmbeddingController#update

adjudication.rationale: `RestAdapter.basePath()` now returns "/admin/" only for types in `ADMIN_MODELS` (after `type.replace('_','-')`). The new singleton model type `embedding` is not in `ADMIN_MODELS`, so its basePath will be `"/"`. The new `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` returns an absolute `pathFor()` of `"/admin/customize/embedding"`. If `RestAdapter` constructs URLs by concatenating `basePath + pathFor` (as its API shape suggests), this becomes `"//admin/customize/embedding"` (scheme-relative), which would break loading/saving of the admin embedding page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing model classes models/embedding.js.es6 and models/embeddable-host.js.es6 — store.find('embedding') and store.createRecord('embeddable-host') resolve to undefined, causing crashes in the route and in _hydrateEmbedded's sideload lookup

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces usage of new client-side types without adding corresponding model definitions: the route calls `this.store.find('embedding')` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin-embedding.js.es6) and the controller calls `this.store.createRecord('embeddable-host')` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6), but the diff adds no `app/assets/javascripts/**/models/embedding.js.es6` or `.../models/embeddable-host.js.es6`. Given Discourse’s pattern of defining a JS model per type for the store to instantiate/serialize, this likely results in the store being unable to resolve these types at runtime (undefined model class / failed lookup), causing crashes when the route loads or when adding a host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757 interpolates host values raw into SQL INSERT, so a stored setting value containing a single quote causes a SQL syntax error that halts db:migrate

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, host strings from the old `site_settings` value are inserted via raw string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. If any host line `h` contains a single quote, the generated SQL becomes invalid (or worse), causing `db:migrate` to fail. The diff shows no escaping/parameterization for `h` before executing the SQL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op endpoint that re-renders the unchanged OpenStruct without persisting, silently losing changes once setting fields are added (advisory)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` just `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without reading params or persisting anything, and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (id + `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`). On the client, `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` against `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` (routes.rb), but there are currently no editable fields on the embedding model in the diff—hosts are persisted via the separate `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` create/update/destroy endpoints. So it’s not a present defect, but it is a real, diff-grounded completeness/architecture concern: the update endpoint and "save changes" action are effectively dead/placeholder and could silently fail once embedding-level settings are added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy raises NoMethodError on nil for nonexistent id, returning 500 instead of 404 (update/create share the pattern via save_host)
Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that only re-renders the serializer, persisting nothing while returning 200, so callers believe settings were saved

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` does not read any params or persist anything; it just `render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, ...)` after `fetch_embedding` builds an `OpenStruct` of `EmbeddableHost.all`. On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would receive a 200 response even though nothing is saved. However, this diff also introduces `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` for actual persistence (create/update/destroy per host), and the shown `embedding.hbs` template has no "save changes" button/fields, so this looks more like a misleading/unused no-op endpoint than a clearly broken user-facing behavior demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy crash with NoMethodError (500) via save_host(nil)/host.destroy on nil when the id doesn't exist; should return 404
New REST CRUD surface (embeddable_hosts and embedding controllers) ships with zero behavioral tests; removed allows_embeddable_host? had four examples deleted without equivalent port-scheme coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new admin REST endpoints/controllers for embedding management (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy and Admin::EmbeddingController#show/update) and new client-side CRUD UI, but the only new controller specs merely assert subclassing (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and embedding_controller_spec.rb) with no behavior/CRUD tests. Additionally, the prior SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? test block with multiple scheme variants was removed (spec/models/site_setting_spec.rb); while EmbeddableHost specs cover http/https input and trimming, there isn’t equivalent request-level coverage for the new REST surface or full parity of the old scheme-handling scenarios in the same place.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb interpolates raw site setting values into SQL, so a value containing a single quote aborts db:migrate with a syntax error

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds an INSERT statement via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value `h` comes from the `site_settings` row `embeddable_hosts` and is not quoted/escaped. If `h` contains a single quote, the generated SQL becomes syntactically invalid and will abort `db:migrate` (and it also creates SQL injection risk within the migration context).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration matches category via s.value = c.name against raw setting string, so slug values or case differences silently fall back to uncategorized, losing the admin's chosen category

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the category is derived via a SQL join on `site_settings.value = categories.name` for `s.name = 'embed_category'`. If the prior `embed_category` setting stored something other than the exact category `name` (e.g., a slug-like value, an ID, or a name with different case/changed name), the query returns no rows, `category_id` becomes 0, and the migration falls back to `uncategorized_category_id`, then deletes the old settings. That can silently migrate existing embeddable hosts into the wrong category (data loss of the admin’s intended mapping).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost with a port is stored verbatim but record_for_host compares against URI.host which excludes the port, so host_allowed? returns false for port-specified hosts the admin entered

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, `before_validation` strips scheme and path but leaves the optional port intact (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), so an admin-entered host like `example.com:3000` is stored with `:3000`. But `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host` (which excludes the port) for lookup: `host = uri.host` then `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. As a result, stored `example.com:3000` will not match lookup `example.com`, causing `host_allowed?` to incorrectly return false for port-specified allowed hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contents are swapped, misleading future readers (advisory)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)` (and related) definitions. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/clarity issue (file contents don’t match filenames), but it doesn’t by itself introduce a functional defect since the fabricator names still exist and will load normally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_spec.rb:1404 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test is vacuous because expandable_first_post? no longer consults hosts

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` to no longer check `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` (now only `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`; see `app/models/topic.rb`). In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the example named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" still expects `false` but no longer sets conditions that would make the method true (it doesn’t stub `has_topic_embed?` or set `embed_truncate`), so it will pass regardless and no longer tests host-related behavior. This is a real, diff-grounded test-quality issue, not an app defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed silently drops per-host category when record_for_host returns nil; category lookup uses embed_url host while validation uses referer host, so mismatched CDN/subdomain hosts import into the wrong category

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the per-host category is derived from `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` where `url` is the embed_url being imported (`eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` then `category: eh.try(:category_id)`). Separately, the embed access check in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` validates against the *referer* (`EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`). This creates a verifiable mismatch: if the referer host is allowed but the embed_url host differs (CDN/subdomain/redirect), `record_for_host(url)` can return nil and the category becomes nil/default, silently losing the intended per-host category selection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The contents of embeddable_host_fabricator.rb and category_fabricator.rb are swapped: category_fabricator.rb defines the embeddable_host fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (host + category), while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the various `Fabricator(:category)` definitions that previously lived in `category_fabricator.rb`. This is a real mismatch in file contents vs. expected naming/convention, but it likely won’t break behavior as Fabrication loads fabricators by scanning the directory, not by filename.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is a dead no-op path: it re-serializes @embedding without persisting anything, and the client's saveChanges() sends an empty payload against a route that writes nothing

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Admin::EmbeddingController#update just re-renders the current @embedding without changing/persisting anything (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb). The client controller’s saveChanges() calls this.get('embedding').update({}) with an empty payload (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6), so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route is effectively a no-op. However, the new UI (admin/templates/embedding.hbs) never invokes saveChanges (only addHost / per-host save/delete via embeddable_hosts), so this is dead/unused plumbing rather than a demonstrable broken behavior introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embedding adapter's pathFor() always returns /admin/customize/embedding, so destroyRecord() on an existing host issues a DELETE to an undefined route (404), leaving the row on screen and breaking host deletion from the UI

adjudication.rationale: The new `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` adapter (with `pathFor() { return "/admin/customize/embedding"; }`) applies to the `embedding` model/route (`admin/routes/admin-embedding.js.es6` does `this.store.find('embedding')`). Host deletion in the UI calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord()` where `host` is an `embeddable-host` record (`admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`). The diff adds `embeddable-host` to `ADMIN_MODELS` in `discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6`, causing its REST calls to use the `/admin/` base path, and the Rails routes include `resources :embeddable_hosts` under `/admin` (so DELETE `/admin/embeddable_hosts/:id` is defined). Nothing in the diff indicates `destroyRecord()` for an embeddable-host would use the embedding adapter or hit `/admin/customize/embedding`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The basePath change (type.replace('_', '-')) in the store silently alters path construction for every future model with an underscore, introducing hidden coupling just to satisfy the embeddable-host model name

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6`, `basePath` now does `type.replace('_', '-')` before checking `ADMIN_MODELS`. This is a cross-cutting behavior change: it introduces implicit normalization of model names for *any* type containing `_` (even though it only replaces the first underscore), and it changes how future entries in `ADMIN_MODELS` must be named/expected. The diff doesn’t show an immediate breakage from this, but the finding’s “hidden coupling” concern is grounded in the new comparison logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The admin UI write path (create/update/delete of hosts via the adapter) is entirely untested; added specs are only AdminController subclass smoke tests, leaving the real route contract unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a full admin write surface for embeddable hosts (Ember component actions calling `host.save()` / `destroyRecord()` in `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, plus Rails endpoints `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy` wired via `resources :embeddable_hosts`). However, the only new controller specs are smoke tests asserting the controllers subclass `Admin::AdminController` (`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb`, `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) and do not exercise the create/update/destroy JSON contract (params shape `params[:embeddable_host]`, returned serializer root `embeddable_host`, error handling, category fallback, etc.). Existing/new tests cover model trimming/allow logic and embed behavior, but not the admin UI write path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embedding_controller.rb update endpoint accepts PUT but only re-renders the payload without persisting anything (no write, no parameter read), so admin saves have no effect

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` indeed just re-renders the serialized embedding object and does not read params or persist anything (`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`). However, the added UI for managing allowed hosts saves/deletes via the separate `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`host.save(props)` hits `/admin/embeddable_hosts/:id`), and the added `embedding.hbs` template does not invoke `saveChanges` at all. So the PUT endpoint looks like an unused/placeholder route (and `saveChanges` looks like dead code), but the diff does not show a user-facing “save” that is currently broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Port format drift in EmbeddableHost: validation allows and stores 'example.com:8080' but record_for_host compares URI#host (port stripped), so hosts saved with ports can never match referers

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and `before_validation` strips scheme and path but does not strip the port, so a record can be saved as `example.com:8080` (see `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`). However `record_for_host` parses the referer/url with `URI(...)` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, and `URI#host` does not include the port. This means stored hosts with ports will never match referers, so `host_allowed?` will incorrectly return false for such entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No index on host column (or lower(host)) in embeddable_hosts table while the lookup runs per embed request with a non-sargable lower(host) = ? predicate, replacing a cached in-memory setting check

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces DB-backed host allowlisting via `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which calls `record_for_host` and performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). This lookup is now used on embed requests (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`) and in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, replacing the prior in-memory `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` check. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts(host, category_id, ...)` but adds no index on `host` (nor functional index on `lower(host)`), making the predicate potentially non-indexable and a likely performance regression, though not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host returns false (boolean) instead of nil for 'no record', so future callers using 'if rec = record_for_host(url)' will crash or misroute when lookup fails

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns `false` on malformed/blank URI/host and an AR object or `nil` when no row matches (`where(...).first`). In Ruby, `false` is falsy just like `nil`, so an idiom like `if rec = record_for_host(url)` will not crash or misroute; it simply won’t enter the branch when `false` is returned. Existing callers shown are also safe: `host_allowed?` uses `.present?` (false.present? => false) and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` (false.try(...) => nil in Rails). The claimed crash behavior is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: category_id is null: false with no foreign key, so deleting a category leaves dead category_ids that fail at import time instead of being prevented at write time

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts.category_id` as `null: false` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) and the model declares `belongs_to :category` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb), but the diff does not add any DB-level foreign key constraint or any app-level protection/cascade behavior on category deletion. That means a category can be deleted while rows in `embeddable_hosts` still reference its id, leaving orphaned `category_id` values. This is a real data-integrity concern introduced by the new table, though the claim about it definitively "fail[ing] at import time" is not fully provable from the diff alone (it depends on how `PostCreator` handles an invalid category id).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No UNIQUE constraint on host, allowing duplicate host rows from concurrent inserts

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `embeddable_hosts` table (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) with `t.string :host, null: false` but no unique index/constraint, and the model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has a format validation but no `validates_uniqueness_of :host`. This allows duplicate rows for the same host (including via concurrent inserts), and later logic like `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(...).first` can return an arbitrary matching row, leading to inconsistent category selection for embeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host canonicalization is split between before_validation callback (normalize-on-write) and lookup lower(host) (normalize-on-read) with no downcase normalization on write, so bypassing the callback stores unnormalized values
admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first with no nil guard, so a bad id causes nil.host= NoMethodError 500 instead of a 4xx response

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. `save_host` immediately dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`), so if the id is invalid/missing and `host` is `nil`, it will raise a `NoMethodError` and return a 500 instead of a 404/4xx. This is directly verifiable in the diff. (The same nil risk also exists in `#destroy`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic.rb:869 expandable_first_post? dropped the embeddable host check, so first-post expansion now occurs even when no embeddable hosts are configured, changing feature behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the previous gating condition in `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). With embeddable hosts now modeled via `EmbeddableHost` records (and the `embeddable_hosts` site setting removed), this means expandable-first-post behavior no longer depends on any “hosts configured” check. That is a real, diff-grounded behavior change, but the diff doesn’t establish it’s incorrect—showing expansion for already-embedded topics even if no hosts are currently configured could be intentional—so it’s better treated as a non-bug review concern to confirm intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_spec.rb:1402 test is vacuous because has_topic_embed? is unstubbed, so it never exercises the removed host guard

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` under `describe "expandable_first_post?"`, the example `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` does not stub `topic.has_topic_embed?` or set `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true`. Since `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, the test will return false by default (because `embed_truncate` defaults false and/or `has_topic_embed?` is false on a built topic), making it effectively vacuous and not actually asserting anything about embeddable hosts/removed guard logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:61 'embeddable hosts not set' error replaced by generic 'invalid referer host', leaving admins without a diagnosable error for empty host table misconfiguration

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` removed the explicit empty-config check (`raise ... 'embeddable hosts not set' if SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?`) and now only raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('invalid referer host')` when `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` is false. With an empty `embeddable_hosts` table, `host_allowed?` will return false and the error becomes the generic 'invalid referer host', eliminating the more diagnosable message for the specific misconfiguration case. This is a real, diff-grounded review concern but not a functional defect (access is still denied).

adjudication_records.issue_text: migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb interpolates raw host values into SQL INSERT, crashing on values containing single quotes (e.g. eviltrout.com's-blog); should escape or use sanitize_sql

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If a host value `h` contains a single quote, the SQL becomes invalid and will crash during migration; it also creates SQL injection risk. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embedding_controller.rb update action is a no-op that re-renders show while client saveChanges() PUTs to it, giving a false impression of persistence; should be removed or made to actually save

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders the current `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`) without persisting anything (no settings updates, no host changes) (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb). The client controller defines `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6), which would issue a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` via the new adapter. However, in the provided template (`embedding.hbs`) there is no Save button/wire-up to `saveChanges`, and host persistence is handled via `embeddable-host` saves/deletes, so this is more an incomplete/placeholder endpoint than a demonstrable broken behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6:200 plural branch 'obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []' doesn't guard against null entries from _lookupSubType, unlike the singular branch, causing possible client crashes on partial side-loaded payloads

adjudication.rationale: In store.js.es6 `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural handling (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/`) maps each id via `_lookupSubType` and then unconditionally assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `map` always returns an array, `|| []` never removes missing lookups, so the array can contain `null`/`undefined` entries when side-loaded records are absent. Unlike the singular branch (which only sets `obj[subType]` when `hydrated` is truthy), the plural branch deletes the original `*_ids` field and replaces it with a possibly sparse array, which can plausibly break client code that assumes array elements are valid records (e.g., calling `.get(...)` during iteration).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection via string interpolation in data migration db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:23 — unescaped host values terminate the string literal and inject SQL; must use parameterized insert

adjudication.rationale: The migration builds an INSERT statement via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The `h` value comes from `site_settings.value` (previous `embeddable_hosts`) and is not escaped/quoted safely, so a host containing a `'` (or crafted SQL) can break the string literal and alter the executed SQL. This is a real SQL-injection / migration-corruption risk; it should use parameterization/quoting (e.g., `quote(h)` or bound params) instead of raw interpolation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: destroy in app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:16-19 calls host.destroy on possibly-nil record, causing 500 NoMethodError instead of 404 for bad id

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy` without checking for `nil`. If an invalid/nonexistent `:id` is passed, `host` will be `nil` and this will raise a `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb → save_host(nil) → nil.host= raises NoMethodError for nonexistent id, same nil-handling issue as destroy

Normalization mismatch in app/models/embeddable_host.rb:16 — lookup compares lower(host) against un-downcased uri.host, silently breaking embedding for hosts stored with uppercase letters; downcase both sides
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same case-insensitivity bug: the query lower(host) = ? intends a case-insensitive match but the input host/uri.host parameter isn’t downcased, so mixed/upper-case hosts can fail to match. Candidate explicitly recommends downcasing both sides.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Port-scoping drift: validation regex permits :port suffix on stored hosts but record_for_host matches only uri.host, so stored ports are dead input; either strip ports or compare host+port

adjudication.rationale: In EmbeddableHost, the validation regex allows an optional ":port" suffix (app/models/embeddable_host.rb: /\A...(:[0-9]{1,5})?...\Z/i) and the before_validation callback strips scheme and path but does not strip ports. However, record_for_host parses the input URL and compares only uri.host (no port) via where("lower(host) = ?", host). If a record is saved as "example.com:8080", then host_allowed?("http://example.com:8080") will look up "example.com" and fail to match, making stored ports ineffective and breaking expected allowlisting behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Swapped fabricator bodies: category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains category fabricators, risking wrong-file edits or duplicate Fabricator(:category) definitions

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (and no longer defines `:category`), while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the `Fabricator(:category)` plus related category fabricators (`:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/clarity issue (definitions are in unexpectedly named files), but the diff does not by itself prove a runtime break or an actual duplicate `Fabricator(:category)` definition—only that it could confuse future edits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController spec only asserts subclassing and doesn't exercise save_host logic, including param parsing, blank category_id fallback, and render_json_error path

adjudication.rationale: The new spec `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` only checks `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController` and does not cover any of the nontrivial controller behavior added in `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`, including `save_host`’s parameter usage (`params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, `:category_id`), the fallback to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` when `category_id.blank?`, and the failure branch `render_json_error(host)` when `host.save` fails. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update/destroy in EmbeddableHostsController call methods on EmbeddableHost.where(...).first which is nil for a bad id, causing NoMethodError and a 500
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes that update/destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(...).first and then call methods on the result without handling nil, leading to NoMethodError/500 for invalid IDs. This is the same missing-record validation problem as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController spec only asserts subclassing; show/update serialization and lack of persistence in update are untested, so saving embedding settings silently loses them

adjudication.rationale: The new specs for `Admin::EmbeddingController` and `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` only assert subclassing and do not exercise the new endpoints/serialization (e.g., `Admin::EmbeddingController#show/#update` just `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`). Also, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does not persist anything (it simply re-renders the same OpenStruct model), so if the client were to call the PUT route expecting settings to be saved, that would be a no-op. However, in the diff the UI primarily saves hosts via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and there’s no clear template usage of `saveChanges`, so the “silently loses them” impact is not directly demonstrated as a concrete runtime bug from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test is vacuous since the embeddable_hosts.present? conjunct was removed from expandable_first_post?

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` conjunct from `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (topic.rb now only checks `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). In `topic_spec`, the test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer sets `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` (and that setting is no longer consulted anyway), so it will pass simply because defaults (e.g., `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` default false) or `has_topic_embed?` being false make the method return false regardless of embeddable host presence. This is a real, diff-grounded test quality issue rather than an application defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic spec's true-case fabricates an embeddable_host the new code never consults, mirroring the removed implementation instead of the spec

adjudication.rationale: In `Topic#expandable_first_post?` the host check was removed (`SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && ...` -> `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`), so the existence of an `EmbeddableHost` record is no longer consulted for this method. However, `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` still has a context `describe 'with an emeddable host'` that does `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` before asserting the true case; the test passes because it also sets `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` and stubs `has_topic_embed?`, making the fabricated host irrelevant. This is misleading/unnecessary test setup rather than a functional bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contents were swapped during the file move

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (host + category), while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)` plus related category variants (`:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). So the contents were effectively swapped relative to the filenames. This is a real, diff-grounded issue (misnamed/misplaced fabricators) but not necessarily a functional defect if the test suite loads all fabricator files via a directory glob.

adjudication_records.issue_text: camelCase-to-underscored model-type normalization for embeddable-host in rest.js.es6 has no test coverage, risking 404s on admin embedding CRUD if regressed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial normalization logic in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6` (`type.replace('_', '-')`) so admin base paths match `ADMIN_MODELS` entries like `'embeddable-host'`. There is no test in the diff that exercises `RestAdapter.basePath` behavior for an underscored type (e.g. `embeddable_host`) or otherwise verifies admin CRUD routing won’t 404 if this mapping regresses. While the finding’s wording mentions camelCase→underscored (the code is underscore→dash), the underlying point—new normalization without explicit coverage—is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No JS-side tests exist for the new embeddable-host component, admin-embedding controller/route, or embedding adapter, leaving save/cancel/delete flows unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new admin Ember code for embedding management (adapter `app/assets/javascripts/admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6`, route `admin/routes/admin-embedding.js.es6`, controller `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`, and component + template `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` / `admin/templates/components/embeddable-host.hbs`) implementing nontrivial UI actions (edit/save/cancel/delete with AJAX via `host.save`, `destroyRecord`, `bootbox.confirm`, buffering). The only JS tests changed/added in this diff are for the generic store embedding behavior (`test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6` and pretender fixtures), and there are no JS-side tests covering the new admin embedding flows/components. This is a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap rather than a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :embeddable_hosts uses force: true in a shipped numbered migration, which drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table on re-run, destroying migrated data

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which will drop and recreate the table if it already exists. That can silently destroy any existing `embeddable_hosts` data in scenarios where the migration is re-run or the table pre-exists (e.g., partial/failed deploy or manual table creation), whereas omitting `force: true` would fail safely instead of deleting data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: execute query for 'embed_category' setting crashes with NoMethodError when the setting is at its default (row absent), so [0] is nil — migration fails to apply; same crash at lines 13-15 for uncategorized_category_id
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the migration indexing into execute(...)[0]['id'] without handling the case where the query returns no rows (default/absent embed_category setting), causing a nil/NoMethodError crash and failing the migration (and related feature flow).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unconditional DELETE of site_settings rows at line 30 runs even when the insert of migrated hosts is skipped or fails, destroying the old host list with nothing migrated

adjudication.rationale: In the migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb), the final `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings ..."` does run unconditionally, but the insert is only “skipped” when `embeddable_hosts` is missing/blank (so there is nothing meaningful to migrate). If an insert actually fails (e.g., SQL error), the migration would raise and stop before reaching the DELETE, and in transactional DBs the whole migration would roll back. So the specific claim that it can delete an existing host list “when the insert is skipped or fails” leaving “nothing migrated” is not supported by what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host values are interpolated raw into the INSERT (SQL injection/crash on single quotes) and legacy entries with schemes/paths are stored unnormalized, so they never match record_for_host's lower(host) lookup
matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that legacy host entries containing schemes/paths are inserted via raw SQL without normalization and therefore won’t match the later host lookup logic (e.g., record_for_host comparing normalized/lowercased bare host). That is the same underlying issue as the golden comment, though it additionally mentions SQL injection concerns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent reclassification: if embed_category can't be matched by name, migrated hosts silently get uncategorized_category_id, with no backfill possible since settings rows are deleted

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration derives category_id by joining site_settings.value to categories.name for the 'embed_category' setting; if no match is found it falls back to uncategorized_category_id (category_id == 0 branch). It then inserts embeddable_hosts rows using that category_id and finally deletes the 'embeddable_hosts' and 'embed_category' site_settings rows. This means a non-matching embed_category value will silently map all migrated hosts to uncategorized, and the original setting value is removed so you cannot later backfill/recover the intended category from settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No down/rollback restores the deleted site_settings rows, making the migration irreversible and non-rollbackable on failed deploy

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` is defined with `def change` but contains non-reversible operations: raw `execute(...)` SQL inserts and `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Rails cannot auto-rollback these, and there is no `down` method to restore deleted `site_settings` rows, so rollback would be impossible/lose that data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead guard: embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0 calls a PG::Result method on an ActiveRecord::Result, raising NoMethodError and crashing the migration instead of skipping the insert

adjudication.rationale: The migration does call `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` on the return value of `execute("SELECT ...")`, but the finding asserts (without support from the diff) that `execute` returns an `ActiveRecord::Result` that lacks `cmd_tuples` and would crash. From the diff alone we can’t verify the runtime type/behavior of `execute` in this codebase/AR version (and on PostgreSQL it commonly returns a `PG::Result` which *does* respond to `cmd_tuples`, and `cmd_tuples` is not a “dead guard” there).

adjudication_records.issue_text: destroy/update in admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb call .destroy/save_host on nil record when params[:id] doesn't match, producing a 500 instead of a 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If no record matches, `host` is `nil`. `update` then calls `save_host(host)` which immediately dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`), and `destroy` calls `host.destroy`; both will raise `NoMethodError` and return a 500 rather than a 404/handled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: params[:embeddable_host][:host] unwrap in admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb raises NoMethodError (500) when the envelope or :host/:category_id key is missing, where a 400 belongs; EmbeddableHost#before_validation also raises on nil host
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that EmbeddableHost#before_validation calls `self.host.sub!` and will raise NoMethodError when `host` is nil. The candidate explicitly mentions this same model callback problem (“EmbeddableHost#before_validation also raises on nil host”), even though it also adds an additional controller params-unwrapping issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: delete() in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no rejection handler on destroyRecord(), so failed deletes are invisible to the user and the row stays in the table

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete() action calls this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...), but there is no .catch(...) (unlike save(), which uses .catch(popupAjaxError)). If the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled, no error is shown to the user, and deleteHost is never sent—so the row remains in the table with no feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Optimistic state mutation in embeddable-host.js.es6 sets host.category from the client-side chosen id instead of the server response, so a server-coerced blank category_id (mapped to uncategorized) causes displayed vs. stored state divergence

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6#save`, after `host.save(props)` the code forcibly does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` based on the client-side `categoryId`. But the server (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) explicitly coerces a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. Since `cantSave` doesn’t require `categoryId` to be present, `categoryId` can be null/blank, leading to the server persisting uncategorized while the client sets `category` to `findById(null)` (likely `undefined`), creating a displayed vs stored divergence until reload (and also overriding any other server-side coercion).

adjudication_records.issue_text: A host saved with an explicit port passes validation but can never match a referer, since record_for_host compares host without port against uri.host, silently rejecting embeds

adjudication.rationale: In EmbeddableHost, the validation regex allows storing hosts with an explicit port (e.g. "example.com:3000"), and the before_validation callback strips scheme/path but does not strip the port. However, record_for_host parses the referer URL with URI(host) and compares `uri.host` (which excludes the port) against `embeddable_hosts.host` via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. Thus a saved record like "example.com:3000" will never match a referer such as "http://example.com:3000/..." (uri.host == "example.com"), causing embeds to be rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ADVISORY: saveChanges() in admin-embedding.js.es6 fires update({}) with no .catch, making any future failure (or a 403) silent

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`, the `saveChanges()` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` and does not attach any error handling (no `.catch(popupAjaxError)` or similar). While the diff doesn’t show this action being invoked from `embedding.hbs` (there’s no save button wired to `saveChanges`), the lack of a catch is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness issue: if this action is later used and the update request fails (e.g., 403), the UI won’t surface an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ADVISORY: record_for_host returning nil causes embedded topics to silently fall into the default category via try(:category_id) with no log line for the fallback

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the category is set to `eh.try(:category_id)` (where `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`). But the diff also changes host validation to rely on `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (via `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`), and `host_allowed?` is defined as `record_for_host(host).present?`. So if `record_for_host` returns nil, the request/import should be blocked earlier as an invalid host rather than “silently falling back” to some default category. Also, the claim that it falls into the “default category” is not verifiable from this diff because `PostCreator` behavior when `category: nil` isn’t shown here.
